title: ReAct and Reflexion: How Agents Think Before They Act — and Learn From Failing
summary: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) interleaves explicit reasoning traces with tool calls: the model writes a thought, takes an action, observes the result, and writes the next thought with that observation in context. It's the loop underneath almost every tool-using agent today, precisely because it makes the model's intermediate reasoning legible and correctable. Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) builds on top of it: when an attempt fails, the agent writes a verbal self-critique of what went wrong, stores it in an episodic memory buffer, and retries with that reflection injected into context — a form of reinforcement learning that updates behavior without touching any weights.
key_learning: Reflexion only helps when the agent has a reliable failure signal — a test suite, an evaluator, a scorable outcome. Without one, the self-critique step just produces plausible-sounding excuses instead of an actual correction, and retries don't improve.
